purpose: Every place repository code (src/ and tools/) starts a child process, with whether a default-selection test reaches it and whether its child can reach the host keyring (#661, the helper-owned residual of #540). tests/support/helper_launch_inventory.py reads the sources; tests/unit/tools/test_helper_launch_keyring.py fails for a launch function that is not listed here, for a changed launch count, and for a verdict its checks cannot confirm. Launches written in tests/ are the sites of run_context_child_sites.json, not these.

census.method: A pytest plugin (kept in the p661 review kit) replaced the Windows process-creation call for the whole default selection, allowed git, refused every other child, and recorded for each launch the test, the command, the child's environment (whether it names a keyring backend) and the repository frames on the stack; for a Python child it also computed the child program's import closure. No refused child started, so none could reach any credential store.
census.head: 2df6fec
census.selection: the default selection of every test file under tests/ (pyproject addopts -m expression): 15793 tests passed in three runs (92 files that name a launching module, the other 474 test files, tests/e2e); 442 failed and 55 errored because a refused launch is not the launch they expect
census.result: Besides git, the launches a default-selection test reaches are: the Plan 11.26 measurement child (product code that reaches keyring, selects fail in its own environment, controlled), nested pytest sessions (the root conftest installs fail), `python -m evidence_handoff_runtime.service_cli` (its closure imports no keyring), the plan 12 contained probe (inherits the environment; controlled), and test-authored programs started through a helper (`caller_program`: each recorded closure imports no keyring).
census.limits: A test that hit a refused launch stopped there, so a later launch in the same test is not in the census (for example current_identity after resolve_client in the Stage C tests; its reach was added by reading the test). Git is allowed through and identified from the command text, and a git child's own descendants (hooks) are not observed; a shell child (bash in the Stage C tests) is recorded but not classified, and its startup files are the host's. Windows only: a launch a Linux-only test makes is for PR CI. The scan reads Python only: .ps1 and .sh runner scripts are outside it, and so are aliased module names and reflective lookups (the guard's inventory documents this). A test outside the default selection is outside the census by definition.

verdicts.non_python: Every launch in the function starts a fixed tool (`tools`: git, docker, powershell, or acpx for `--version`), which runs none of this repository's Python. The guard checks each tool name appears in the function.
verdicts.closure_clear: The child runs a fixed module or script of the repository. The guard recomputes its import closure (tests.support.child_keyring.import_closure) from the sources: no module imports keyring, and nothing is computed or unresolved.
verdicts.nested_pytest: The child is a pytest session over this repository's tests; it loads the root conftest, which installs keyring's fail backend (#538). Its own launches are sites of run_context_child_sites.json. The guard checks the function builds a pytest command.
verdicts.controlled: The child can reach keyring, or its closure cannot be bounded, and a test applies a control (tests/support/child_keyring.py) for its duration. The guard fails for any test module that names one of `entry_calls` without the control.
verdicts.caller_program: The program is the caller's argument, not one the function chooses (the guard checks no launch here names sys.executable). A child reaches keyring only if the caller names product code. The default-selection tests that reach it (`reached_by`, from the census) name programs of their own, and the census closure of each imports no keyring.
verdicts.not_reached: No default-selection test starts the child (`reason` says what the tests do instead). The function stays listed so a test that begins to reach it is a visible change in review; the guard cannot see a new reach, only that the verdict is recorded.
verdicts.wrapper: Forwards a launch that another function makes and starts no process of its own; the launch it forwards is classified where it is made. The guard needs the reason.
